question: A 2-week-old newborn girl is brought to the physician for a follow-up examination after the initial newborn examination showed asymmetry of the legs. She was born at term to a 26-year-old woman, gravida 3, para 2. Pregnancy was complicated by a breech presentation and treated with an emergency lower-segment transverse cesarean section. The newborn's head circumference is 35 cm (13.7 in). She is at the 60th percentile for length and 75th percentile for weight. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The spine and overlying skin do not indicate significant abnormalities. Abduction of the right hip after cupping the pelvis and flexing the right hip and knee causes a palpable clunk. The feet exhibit no deformities. Ultrasonography of the hip revealed a 50° angle between the lines along the bone acetabulum and the ilium. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.opa: Immobilize the hips with a spica cast
options.opb: Obtain an MRI of the right hip
options.opc: Obtain an X-ray of the right hip
options.opd: Reassure the mother and schedule follow-up appointment in 4 weeks

paths: (Breech Presentation)-PREDISPOSES->(Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip)-CAUSES->(Disease)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(physiological aspects)-PROCESS_OF->(Hip structure)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Breech presentation" -> "Increased risk of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH)" -> "Possible DDH in newborn" -> 70% CHAIN: "Palpable clunk on hip abduction" -> "Positive Ortolani test" -> "Suspicion of DDH" -> 80% CHAIN: "50° angle on hip ultrasound" -> "Confirmatory finding for DDH" -> "Likelihood of DDH diagnosis" -> 90% CHAIN: "Positive Ortolani test" -> "Indication for further imaging" -> "Need for diagnostic confirmation" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The newborn's presentation with a palpable clunk on hip abduction, positive Ortolani test, and a 50° angle on hip ultrasound indicate a high likelihood of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). The most appropriate next step in management would be to obtain an X-ray of the right hip for further diagnostic confirmation.
analysis: The newborn's presentation with a palpable clunk on hip abduction, positive Ortolani test, and a 50° angle on hip ultrasound strongly suggest developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). The most appropriate next step in management for DDH is to obtain an X-ray of the right hip for further diagnostic confirmation.
